cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has been carrying a message from the LORD: wake up, Jerusalem, because He is redeeming His people. Now the LORD points to someone and calls Him My Servant. The first thing He says is that this Servant will prosper.

cards.question: The LORD says His Servant will prosper. What else does He say will happen to the Servant?

answers.text: He will be lifted up high
He will stay hidden away
He will rule from Babylon

cards.text: Raised. Lifted up. Highly exalted. Friend, that's THREE ways to say UP in one sentence, and then the LORD says something hard: many were appalled at Him.

cards.question: True or false: in Isaiah 52:14, people are appalled at the Servant because of how He looks.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then it flips: He will sprinkle many nations, and KINGS will shut their mouths because of Him. Friend, I can't even get my oven timer to hush.

cards.question: Why do kings shut their mouths because of the Servant?

answers.text: They see what they were never told
They lose a war against Israel
He orders them to keep quiet

cards.text: Now the voice turns to "we": "Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?" Ever drop big news in the group chat and get back… nothing?

cards.question: True or false: the question in Isaiah 53:1 sounds like everybody already believes the message.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then comes a picture of the Servant growing up like a tender shoot, like a root out of dry ground. Not exactly where you'd plant something you want people to notice.

cards.question: Isaiah 53:2 pictures the Servant like a root out of dry ground. What does it say about how He looked?

answers.text: Nothing about Him drew people in
He looked like a king in a palace
Crowds came just to see His face

cards.text: Then it gets heavy: "He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief." I spent years forgotten in a junk drawer, friend, and that doesn't even come close.

cards.question: In Isaiah 53:3, how was the despised Servant treated?

answers.text: Like someone people hide their faces from
Like someone people run to for help
Like someone people crown as their king

cards.text: Now here's the turn. He took up our infirmities, and He carried our sorrows.

cards.question: The Servant carried their sorrows. But what did the speakers in Isaiah 53:4 think was happening to Him?

answers.text: That God had struck Him down
That He was hiding from God
That He was faking His pain

cards.text: And then comes the BUT. He was pierced for our transgressions, and He was crushed for our iniquities.

cards.question: Isaiah 53:5 says the punishment that brought us ___ was upon Him.

answers.text: peace
shame
fear

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah 53:5 says the speakers are healed by the Servant's stripes.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then the speakers own it: we all, like sheep, have gone astray, and each one has turned to his own way. That's me ignoring my GPS while it begs, "Recalculating… RECALCULATING."

cards.question: Isaiah 53:6 says the LORD has laid upon the Servant the ___ of us all.

answers.text: iniquity
care
hope

cards.text: Now watch how He takes it all: "He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth." Me? I bump my gold base on the oven door and the whole Dorinverse hears about it.

cards.question: Isaiah 53:7 compares the silent Servant to which animal?

answers.text: A lamb led to the slaughter
A goat sent into the wilderness
A dove caught in a net

cards.text: As a sheep before her shearers is silent, He stays quiet. By oppression and judgment He was taken away, cut off from the land of the living.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah 53:8 says the Servant was stricken for His own transgression.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Even His grave says something. He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death.

cards.question: The Servant was given a grave with the wicked. What does Isaiah 53:9 say about how He lived?

answers.text: He did no violence and told no lies
He fought back against His enemies
He hid the truth to stay safe

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line in the whole passage: it was the LORD's will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer. But friend, the passage doesn't stop there.

cards.question: Isaiah 53:10 says that when His soul is made a guilt offering, the Servant will see His ___.

answers.text: offspring
enemies
accusers

cards.text: He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand. After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied.

cards.question: In Isaiah 53:11, the LORD calls Him My righteous Servant. What will the Servant do for many?

answers.text: Justify them and bear their iniquities
Judge them and send them away
Teach them and then leave them

cards.text: So the LORD says He will give the Servant a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong. Strong? Friend, I lose wrestling matches to cold cookie dough.

cards.question: Why does the Servant get a portion with the great in Isaiah 53:12?

answers.text: He poured out His life unto death
He won a war against the kings
He built a house for the LORD

cards.text: He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many.

cards.question: True or false: in Isaiah 53:12, the Servant made intercession for the transgressors.

answers.text: True
False

findings.problem: Many choice cards are worded like test questions that point to a verse number instead of pausing mid-story. Examples: "True or false: in Isaiah 52:14…" (stop 1 card 4), "In Isaiah 53:3, how was…" (stop 1 card 12), "Isaiah 53:5 says…" (stop 1 cards 16 and 17), "Isaiah 53:6 says…" (stop 1 card 19), "Isaiah 53:7 compares…" (stop 2 card 2), "Isaiah 53:8 says…" (stop 2 card 4), "Isaiah 53:10 says…" (stop 2 card 8), "In Isaiah 53:11…" (stop 2 card 10), "…in Isaiah 53:12?" (stop 2 card 12), and "in Isaiah 53:12…" (stop 2 card 14). The context in each question should come from the moment (who and what), not from a verse citation.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from the passage before this one: wake up, Jerusalem, and the LORD redeeming His people (Isaiah 52:1, 52:9). The card cites only Isaiah 52:13, so those facts carry no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The statement says people are appalled at the Servant "because of how He looks." Isaiah 52:14 sets the two lines side by side with a dash but never says one causes the other. The baker is marked right for a cause the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke compares the kings to Papa Dorin failing to make his oven timer hush. That makes it about someone silencing someone else. In the text, the kings fall silent at what they see (Isaiah 52:15). The joke also leans toward the wrong answer on card 6, "He orders them to keep quiet."

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The group-chat joke (big news that gets back nothing) already tells the baker the message isn't believed. That gives away the answer to the true or false question on card 8.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Not exactly where you'd plant something you want people to notice" nearly states card 10's answer, "Nothing about Him drew people in." It also rules out the two wrong answers about kingly looks and crowds.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Nothing about Him drew people in," is wider than Isaiah 53:2. The verse speaks only of His form, majesty and beauty: "no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him." The question asks about His looks, but the answer covers everything about Him.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to fill in the exact wording of Isaiah 53:5 ("the punishment that brought us ___"), which they haven't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason toward "peace" over "shame" or "fear."

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
